anomalies.observed: The 5 V output node has a 19k6 resistor (R39) running from the +5V rail down to the NET0007 wire, which is the same net as the FB pin (REG2 pin 24). The intended feedback divider, R75 (6k8) to +5V and R3 (1k3) to GND with its midpoint on FB, is also present. A second top-side resistor on the FB net would change the divider ratio.
anomalies.expected: Specification: "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)" for the MIC26903 5 V rail, with "9A @ 5V max". With only R75/R3 on FB, Vout is about 4.98 V. A 19k6 in parallel with 6k8 on the top leg would give roughly 3.9 V, so R39 should not sit on the FB node.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (1/6): R39 19k6 vertical from +5V junction to NET0007 wire; NET0007 label at FB pin 24; R75 6k8 and R3 1k3 divider; note "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)"
Main buck regulator (5 V rail) ... notes "L = 15uH for 5% ripple current", "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)"

anomalies.impact: If R39 is truly on the FB node, the 5 V rail would regulate to a voltage well below 5 V, starving the servo bank and the 3V3 LDO input. If the wire actually lands on the bootstrap or diode node, the issue is not present, so the finding is uncertain.
